answer:
Solve the 2D small-strain linear elasticity problem in plane stress using FEniCS legacy (dolfin).
Use a vector-valued P2 (second-order Lagrange) displacement space for the displacement field.
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law with unit thickness.
Material properties: E = 70e9 Pa, ν = 0.33, ρ = 2700 kg/m³.
Geometry: parallelogram with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1.2,0.3), (0.2,0.3).
Mesh: a structured triangulation of the parallelogram with exactly 72 triangular cells, built as a 12 × 3 grid (12 divisions along the base direction, 3 along the height) with each grid cell split into two triangles, so that the point (1.1, 0.15) coincides with a mesh node.
Boundary conditions: clamp (fix both displacement components) the entire left inclined edge from (0,0) to (0.2,0.3).
Apply gravity as a body force (0, -ρg) with g = 9.81 m/s² integrated over the domain.
Apply a horizontal point load of magnitude 5000 N in the negative x-direction at the point (1.1, 0.15), applied as a PointSource on the x-component of the displacement field at that location, not smeared over an edge.
Solve the resulting linear system with a direct linear solver.
Compute the in-plane Cauchy stress field from the displacement solution using the plane-stress law.
Compute the von Mises stress from the in-plane stress components (σx, σy, τxy).
Output the displacement field and the von Mises stress distribution over the parallelogram domain.
